collections.summary: Cosmic beginning before the dynastic age.
collections.description: Creation and the opening of cosmic order before the dynastic age.

collections.title: Major Dynasties
collections.summary: Solar, lunar, Yadu, and Kuru houses.
collections.description: Rise of the great houses of epic geography.

collections.title: Birth of Krishna
collections.summary: Kṛṣṇa enters the Yadu world.
collections.description: Kṛṣṇa is born in Mathurā and raised in Vraja.

collections.title: Pandavas
collections.summary: Birth and rise of the five brothers.
collections.description: The five Pāṇḍavas enter the epic world.

collections.title: Mahābhārata Events
collections.summary: Major narrative events of the Mahābhārata — births, exile, the Gītā, and the war — linked across the Knowledge Graph.
collections.description: Events connects people, places, kingdoms, weapons, Gītā chapters, and verses. Each event is a shared Knowledge Graph entity.

collections.title: Cosmic Creation
collections.summary: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, and the first mind-born progenitors.
collections.description: Purāṇic creation opens with Viṣṇu; Brahmā projects the Prajāpatis who seed later lineages. This module stays at the cosmic root — not a merged mega-tree.

collections.title: Kauravas
collections.summary: Birth of Duryodhana's hundred.
collections.description: The Kaurava brothers are born at Hastināpura.

collections.title: Epic Weapons
collections.summary: Bows, astras, maces, conches, and sacred arms of the Mahābhārata — with a few clearly marked weapons from the wider Hindu tradition.
collections.description: A cited catalog of arms from the shared Knowledge Graph. Mahābhārata weapons are listed first; broader Hindu arms (such as the Vajra and Triśūla) are marked separately.

collections.title: Mahābhārata Atlas
collections.summary: Interactive map of kingdoms, cities, forests, rivers and sacred places of the Mahābhārata world.
collections.description: Phase 1 Atlas layer — Mahābhārata-era geography only. Places are shared Knowledge Graph entities; Atlas visualizes, Encyclopedia explains. Approximate modern locations are educational context, not survey precision.

collections.title: Major Mahabharata Events
collections.summary: From the lacquer house to the field of war.
collections.description: Core narrative from the lacquer house through the end of the war.

collections.title: Gītā Concepts
collections.summary: Core philosophical concepts of the Bhagavad Gītā — dharma, karma, bhakti, yoga, and the Self — linked across the Knowledge Graph.
collections.description: Core philosophical ideas of the Bhagavad Gītā — dharma, karma, bhakti, yoga, and the Self — with verses, chapters, and related figures from the shared Knowledge Graph.

collections.title: Bhagavad Gita
collections.summary: The discourse on the field of dharma.
collections.description: Kṛṣṇa teaches Arjuna between the armies at Kurukṣetra.

collections.title: Aftermath
collections.summary: Sacrifice, grief, and the closing of the age.
collections.description: Horse sacrifice, mourning, and the close of the age.

collections.title: Trimūrti
collections.summary: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva with consorts and children.
collections.description: Creation, sustenance and dissolution — with Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Gaṇeśa and Kārttikeya. Variant birth narratives are marked, not flattened.

collections.title: Persons & Deities
collections.summary: Gods, sages, kings, asuras and epic heroes.
collections.description: Figures of Hindu tradition — deities, avatars, ṛṣis, kings and asura lineages — as first-class encyclopedia entities.

collections.title: Major Devīs
collections.summary: Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, Pārvatī, Gaṅgā and related forms.
collections.description: Principal goddesses attested in Purāṇa and epic, kept as a Devī module rather than mixed into male dynastic trees.

collections.title: Prajāpatis
collections.summary: Mind-born sons of Brahmā who seed later races.
collections.description: Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12 lists the mānasaputras. Counts vary across Manu Smṛti and epic redactions — recorded as variant tradition on Brahmā.

collections.title: Places
collections.summary: Cities, rivers and sacred fields.
collections.description: Geographic and sacred places linked to dynasties and events.

collections.title: Manus
collections.summary: Vaivasvata Manu — Manu of the present age.
collections.description: Only the current Manu (Vaivasvata) is expanded here with verified links to Vivasvān and Ikṣvāku. Other Manus can be added when each citation is locked.

collections.title: Saptarṣis
collections.summary: The seven seers associated with Brahmā's mind-born line.
collections.description: Lists of Saptarṣis shift by manvantara. Divine shows the Bhāgavata mānasaputra set used as the working Vaivasvata baseline.

collections.title: Concepts
collections.summary: Dharma, karma, bhakti, jñāna, yoga, ātman, and related ideas.
collections.description: Philosophical and religious concepts cited to scripture — also available as the dedicated Concepts module.

collections.title: Devas
collections.summary: Kaśyapa → Aditi → the Ādityas (Indra, Vivasvān, and kin).
collections.description: Devas are not Asuras. This module follows Kaśyapa and Aditi into the Āditya catalogue of Viṣṇu and Bhāgavata Purāṇas.

collections.title: Asuras
collections.summary: Daityas and Dānavas — the principal Asura houses. Open Daityas or Dānavas for the full separate trees.
collections.description: In Purāṇic taxonomy, Asura is an umbrella for the lineages of Diti (Daityas) and Danu (Dānavas). Rākṣasas are a separate race (Pulastya → Rāvaṇa) and are not merged here. This hub shows both Asura houses side by side; dive into Daityas or Dānavas for the dedicated spines.

faq.question: Are Daityas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas the same?
faq.answer: No. Daityas are children of Diti; Dānavas of Danu; Rākṣasas (e.g. Rāvaṇa) descend from Pulastya through Viśravas. Divine keeps three separate modules so the trees are never mixed.

faq.question: Where is Prahlāda / Bali / Rāvaṇa?
faq.answer: Prahlāda and Bali are under Daityas (and this Asuras hub). Rāvaṇa is under Rākṣasas — not Asuras.

collections.title: Daityas
collections.summary: Kaśyapa → Diti → Hiraṇyakaśipu line through Bali and Bāṇa.
collections.description: Daityas are the children of Diti — kept strictly separate from Dānavas and Rākṣasas. Includes Siṃhikā and Rāhu (Daitya mother; Dānava father).

collections.title: Dynasties
collections.summary: Royal and celestial lineages.
collections.description: Dynasty entities linking persons across modules.

collections.title: Dānavas
collections.summary: Kaśyapa → Danu → Vipracitti and listed Dānava sons.
collections.description: Dānavas descend from Danu. Only figures with Purāṇic or epic support are included — Vipracitti, Puloman, Namuci, Śambara, Maya.

collections.title: Rākṣasas
collections.summary: Pulastya → Viśravas → Rāvaṇa and siblings (separate from Daitya/Dānava).
collections.description: Rākṣasa genealogy is independent: Pulastya's line through Viśravas and Kaikasī. Kubera (Yakṣa) appears as half-brother, not reclassified as Rākṣasa. Not merged into the Asuras module.

collections.title: Scriptures & Verses
collections.summary: Scripture and verse stubs linked into the graph.
collections.description: Thin scripture/verse entities that point at the Gita reader without duplicating text.

collections.title: Nāgas
collections.summary: Kaśyapa → Kadrū → Ananta, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and principal Nāgas.
collections.description: Nāgas are a separate Kaśyapa–Kadrū lineage. Lists of principal serpents follow Bhāgavata and Mahābhārata catalogues.

collections.title: Yakṣas
collections.summary: Kubera, lord of Yakṣas — linked but not merged into Rākṣasas.
collections.description: Sparse by design: Kubera is securely attested as Yakṣa sovereign and half-brother of Rāvaṇa. Further Yakṣa names await verified parentage before inclusion.

collections.title: Gandharvas
collections.summary: Named Gandharvas with epic/Gītā attestation — no invented pedigree.
collections.description: Citraratha is included from Mahābhārata and Bhagavad Gītā 10.26. Parentage is left unset where primary sources do not fix it.

collections.title: Solar Dynasty
collections.summary: Vivasvān → Vaivasvata Manu → Ikṣvāku → Raghu → Daśaratha.
collections.description: A verified spine of the Ikṣvāku line. Intermediate kings are omitted until each link is individually cited — accuracy over a dense unverified ladder.

collections.title: Lunar Dynasty
collections.summary: Atri → Candra → Budha → Purūravas → Yayāti → Yadu / Puru.
collections.description: Origin of the Lunar line and the fork into Yādava and Paurava branches. Long intermediate reigns are marked as traditional descendant links, not invented father–son steps.

collections.title: Raghu Dynasty
collections.summary: Raghu → Aja → Daśaratha → Rāma and brothers.
collections.description: Focused Raghuvaṃśa module overlapping the Solar spine from Raghu through Rāma's generation.

collections.title: Yadu Dynasty
collections.summary: Yayāti → Yadu → Vasudeva → Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma.
collections.description: Yādava line into the Vṛṣṇi house of Vasudeva. Intermediate names between Yadu and Vasudeva are not fabricated.

collections.title: Kuru Dynasty
collections.summary: Kuru → Śaṃtanu → Bhīṣma / Vicitravīrya → Dhṛtarāṣṭra & Pāṇḍu.
collections.description: Core Kuru house of the Mahābhārata Ādi Parva — including Vyāsa's niyoga and the split into Kaurava and Pāṇḍava houses.

collections.title: Pāṇḍavas
collections.summary: The five brothers, Draupadī, Subhadrā, Abhimanyu and Karṇa.
collections.description: Pāṇḍu's sons by divine fathers, their common wife Draupadī, and close kin. Divine parentage is noted on relationships.

collections.title: Kauravas
collections.summary: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Duryodhana, Duḥśāsana and Duḥśalā.
collections.description: The hundred sons are not enumerated one-by-one; the principal named siblings are included with Ādi Parva citations.

collections.title: Kṛṣṇa's Family
collections.summary: Vasudeva, Devakī, Nanda–Yaśodā, Balarāma, Rukmiṇī and Subhadrā.
collections.description: Birth house and foster house of Kṛṣṇa, plus principal consort Rukmiṇī. Aliases (Govinda, Mādhava, Vāsudeva…) are searchable.

collections.title: Rāma's Family
collections.summary: Daśaratha's queens, the four brothers, Sītā, Lava and Kuśa.
collections.description: Immediate family of Rāma from the Valmīki Rāmāyaṇa — including Janaka as adoptive father of Sītā.

collections.title: Major Ṛṣis
collections.summary: Vasiṣṭha, Vyāsa, Vālmīki, Nārada, Parāśara and kin.
collections.description: Seers who structure epic and Purāṇic transmission. Parentage is stated only where the primary narrative fixes it.

collections.title: Major Kings
collections.summary: Cross-dynasty kings with the strongest scriptural footprints.
collections.description: A curated index of major kings already attested in dynasty modules — not a new invented genealogy.
